I find that if I want the figure to look good, I need to draw it myself. 

I used either Powerpoint or Google Slides to do this. I have a collection of path diagrams in a Powerpoint file - when I want a new diagram, I find the most similar one, copy it and modify it (and then add it to the file).

I haven't updated it for a few years because (a) I don't have an employer  who pays for PowerPoint for me, and I'm not paying it myself ( sad face) and I don't do a great deal of SEM in my work any more (also sad face).

You are welcome to take whatever you find useful in the file. Here's the link: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Rs1Ows1Y4fe5oDSbdaYZMfmeUMBnJpOOhTrUIjRXNOE/edit?usp=sharing  (Just don't assume that anything in it is correct or true or realistic or even finished).

Jeremy

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: Print just structural model
parts:
You can try semPaths() from the semPlot package. With structural = TRUE, you can print the structural part of the latent variables.

``` r
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-17
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
library(semPlot)
mod <-
"
f1 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
f2 =~ x4 + x5 + x6
f3 =~ x7 + x8 + x9
f3 ~ f1 + f2
"
fit <- sem(mod)
dat <- simulateData(parTable(fit), sample.nobs = 200, seed = 1234)
fit <- sem(mod, dat)
p <- semPaths(fit,
              what = "path",
              whatLabels = "est",
              structural = TRUE)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/giMKQ0m.png)<!-- -->

<sup>Created on 2024-02-13 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

The plot from semPlot() is highly customizable, thought it would take some time to get exactly what you want.

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai
